plan.purpose: Independent confirmation of exactly two policy contrasts selected from the 30-repetition pilot, not a new allocation search
plan.reuse: Unchanged pilot Problem, analytic derivatives, five starting points, bounds, higher B0/Bplus arrays, affine complex gains per field, shared interaction/source parameters, and sigma0=1.2931669440932318e-4
plan.budget: Same total acquisition budget as pilot: full four-entry matrices on 45 frequencies, sigma_field=sigma0/sqrt(field_time_fraction); equal detector prefactors, no switching overhead or drift
plan.pairing: Independent standard circular-complex noise per field, truth and repetition; identical draws reused within each candidate/baseline pair and rescaled by their time fractions. Confirmation seed differs from pilot. Different truth pairs use independent draws.
plan.primary_statistic: D_i=(Ua_candidate_i-8)^2-(Ua_baseline_i-8)^2; report mean D, sample SD/sqrt(200), and interval mean D +/- z*SE. Negative D favors candidate.
plan.multiple_comparisons: Exactly two primary contrasts. Bonferroni familywise 95% intervals use per-contrast two-sided 97.5% normal-approximation intervals, z=Phi^-1(0.9875) approximately 2.2414. These are Monte Carlo mean-loss comparisons, not parameter confidence intervals or exact finite-sample coverage.
plan.failed_optimization: Retain every estimate and every start. Report optimizer statuses, bounds, and feasible synthetic-truth objective failures. A contrast containing a retained optimizer failure, bound hit, or truth-objective failure cannot support the primary precision claim without an explicitly separate investigation; no silent deletions or reruns.
plan.secondary_outputs: RMSE and bias for each of the four declared truth/policy cases; all estimates and input/source hashes. No 50:50 contrast, new policy, or empirical allocation optimization.
plan.stopping: Run the fixed 200 repetitions per truth regardless of intermediate result direction. Four disjoint repetition shards with one BLAS thread each.

inherited_pilot_plan.question: Does splitting a fixed acquisition budget between zero and finite field improve interaction inference after independent source directions and affine gains are fitted?
inherited_pilot_plan.time_model: A total budget T is shared among fields. Each field measures the same four complex entries on the same 45 frequencies with equal per-entry dwell allocation. sigma0 is the per-entry circular-complex RMS for allocating all T to one full-matrix field. Allocating fraction f gives sigma_field=sigma0/sqrt(f). Independent equal white detector noise, no switching overhead, drift, or field-dependent noise prefactor is assumed. Charge calibration is known. This is a declared acquisition model, not an apparatus claim.
inherited_pilot_plan.observations: full four-entry matrix only; no comparison with a different per-entry time allocation
inherited_pilot_plan.parameters: g/.8, Ua/8, lambda_readout, lambda_source; source directions shared across fields, independent complex affine source/readout gains in each field
inherited_pilot_plan.pairing: For each truth and repetition one independent standard circular-complex noise array per field is reused across policies, multiplied by that policy's sigma_field. This couples Monte Carlo comparisons, not physical measurements between policies.
inherited_pilot_plan.information: Analytic derivatives; true Gaussian Fisher 2 Re(J^H Sigma^-1 J); project affine gains and both source-direction nuisance columns; report Ua local bound after also fitting g. Local information does not establish confidence coverage or global uniqueness.
inherited_pilot_plan.optimizer: Five frozen starts, all attempts retained; best residual selected even if a status is false, reported honestly. Feasible exact-truth residual is a diagnostic upper bound, not an extra start or fitted estimate.
inherited_pilot_plan.selection: Report all five policies and both truths. Best and minimax choices refer only to this grid, source family, noise model and 30-realization empirical experiment. No predetermined improvement claim. No uniform source-angle robustness claim.
